lost_facts.evidence: Shipped exception (transcript L3620-3625, L3670): `class OutputCapError(ValueError): """..."""` with no custom `__init__`, raised at L3670 as `raise OutputCapError(f"max_output_bytes must be 0 (uncapped) or at least {MIN_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES}, got {max_output_bytes}")` -- a bare message string, so the instance never gets a `.max_bytes` attribute. The only remark that states this requirement is `g2.r1.l-floor-konrad` (#cookbooks, 2025-03-17 09:41: "we hang the offending value on the exception as .max_bytes and the message can keep saying whatever it says"), which the pointer sheet records as 0 hits, and a grep of the full transcript for '.max_bytes', 'hang the offending value', and 'regex the traceback' confirms it: the phrase never appears anywhere in the transcript. A second remark that states the same underlying idea from a different angle, `g2.r1.say26` (#incidents, 2025-03-14, 'the field_validator hands the offending value straight into that error ... ValidationError comes back out carrying its message verbatim'), is also 0 hits and also absent from the transcript verbatim. Root cause: both remarks were excluded by the agent's own keyword filters. Chat digest keywords (L1923): ["truncat","output_cap","max_output_bytes","marker","budget","MIN_MAX","stdout","stderr"," cap","floor"] -- l-floor-konrad's exchange never says 'truncat', 'output_cap', 'max_output_bytes' (only bare 'max_bytes'), 'marker', 'budget', 'MIN_MAX', 'stdout', 'stderr', 'cap' as a distinct word, or 'floor'; say26 never mentions any cap/truncation vocabulary at all (it is phrased as an analogy about 'the batch size check'). Neither the Gitea issue grep, wiki grep, nor mail IMAP search terms (L2953: ["truncat","output_cap","max_output_bytes","elided","OutputCapError","stdout"]) would have caught these two messages either, since both remarks live only in Mattermost. This is a genuine search-strategy near-miss compounded by an unusually well-hidden pair of remarks (the MuSR design's intent), not an inference error -- the agent never had the raw text in view to reason about at all.

search_strategy: Thorough and well-sequenced across all three surfaces. Chat: after a failed regex-escaped digest attempt (L1897-1907), the agent built a keyword-filtered chronological digest across ALL channels (kws: truncat, output_cap, max_output_bytes, marker, budget, MIN_MAX, stdout, stderr, ' cap', floor -- L1923) and read all 258 matching lines in paged chunks (L1947-3417), correctly tracking evolving/reversed decisions chronologically rather than taking the first-seen claim. Wiki: rather than trust /api/search (which the ticket warns does not index comments), the agent enumerated every page id and fetched each one whole via /api/pages/{id}, capturing body+comments for all 231 pages into one file (L1195-1283), which is exactly the route needed to surface the 3 comment-only remarks (l-cross-1, l-rule-4, l-log-nikolai) -- all 3 found. Mail: used IMAP SEARCH with a second keyword list (truncat, output_cap, max_output_bytes, elided, OutputCapError, stdout -- L2953) against the whole admin mailbox, found 33 matching mails, and read every relevant thread with expanded newlines -- all 5 mail remarks found. Gitea issues/PR comments were also dumped and grepped first but returned nothing relevant (L936-978). The one structural weakness: the digest/mail keyword lists were built once, early, around the vocabulary the agent already expected ('cap', 'budget', 'floor', 'truncat'), and were never revisited or widened once gaps were suspected -- so the two remarks (say26, l-floor-konrad) that deliberately avoid that vocabulary (discussing 'the batch size check' and bare 'max_bytes' instead) were invisible to every one of the three keyword-filtered searches and never grepped by their own distinctive phrases ('.max_bytes', 'field_validator', 'regex the traceback').
end_reason: Full success path -- not applicable. Run pushed, merged to main, CI green, release deployed and healthy (confirmed L5160-5194: commit 7a1a785, /opt/sweworld/curator/current symlinked to the release containing output_cap.py and the new model fields, service healthy on port 9100). All provenance facts and 8 of 9 hidden-requirement facts scored 1; only g2.r1.failure_behavior scored 0.
notable: The single lost fact traces to exactly two remarks (g2.r1.l-floor-konrad and g2.r1.say26) that both carry g2.r1.failure_behavior and both scored 0 hits across every search the agent ran -- L3670 shows the exact implementation gap this produces: `raise OutputCapError(f"...got {max_output_bytes}")` with no custom __init__, so `.max_bytes` does not exist on the instance.

The digest keyword list is visible at L1923: ['truncat','output_cap','max_output_bytes','marker','budget','MIN_MAX','stdout','stderr',' cap','floor']. Neither missed remark contains any of these terms; l-floor-konrad uses 'max_bytes' (not 'max_output_bytes') and never says 'cap' as a standalone word, and say26 never mentions capping/truncation vocabulary at all, discussing the concept only via an analogy ('the batch size check').

Beyond the missing .max_bytes attribute, the shipped code also never adds a `@field_validator`/floor check to `CodeExecutionBackendConfig` itself (L3849-3907 shows only `Field(default=..., ge=0)`, no floor validator) -- so `CodeExecutionBackendConfig(max_output_bytes=8)` alone does not raise. This second gap traces to the same missing remarks: say26 is the one that names this specifically as a pydantic field_validator, and without it the agent implemented the floor check only at `SandboxCodeExecutionBackend.__init__` (L3946), which is a plausible but distinct reading of the vaguer 'refuse it at construction' remarks it did find (l-floor-emil, l-floor-dario).

Wiki strategy is a strong positive example: rather than rely on /api/search (which the ticket itself warns does not index comments), the agent enumerated and fetched all 231 pages whole, which is precisely the technique needed and is why all 3 wiki-comment remarks were found.

All 4 herrings were correctly identified as superseded before the agent committed to any behaviour; the shipped code follows every one of the 4 reversals and none of the 4 herrings (verified against the final diffs of output_cap.py and types.py).
